thread.old_title: The women who followed from Galilee — at the cross, at the burial, and first at the empty tomb (Luke 8; John 20; Deuteronomy 19)
thread.title: The women who followed from Galilee — at the cross, at the burial, and first at the empty tomb (Luke 8; John 20; Deuteronomy 19)
thread.old_summary:
It ain't new. The same women are at every station. They had followed him from Galilee and kept him out of their own means:

*And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils,* (Luke 8:2)

*And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance.* (Luke 8:3)

They stood at the cross when the twelve were gone:

*And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee, ministering unto him:* (Matthew 27:55)

*Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.* (Matthew 27:56)

*Now there stood by the cross of Yahusha (Jesus) his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.* (John 19:25)

They sat at the burial:

*And there was Mary Magdalene, and the other Mary, sitting over against the sepulchre.* (Matthew 27:61)

And they came first to the tomb and were the first told, the first sent, and the first he met:

*In the end of the sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.* (Matthew 28:1)

*And go quickly, and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and, behold, he goeth before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him: lo, I have told you.* (Matthew 28:7)

*And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9)

*Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* (Matthew 28:10)

Mark says it outright, and John tells what Mary was given to carry:

*Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.* (Mark 16:9)

*Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my Elohim (God), and your Elohim (God).* (John 20:17)

*Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen Yahusha (Lord), and that he had spoken these things unto her.* (John 20:18)

*Go tell my brethren*: the first witness of the rising is a woman carrying the word to the men. The Torah establishes a matter at the mouth of two or three witnesses, and there were two Marys at the tomb, the same two who had sat at the grave and stood at the cross:

*One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.* (Deuteronomy 19:15)

Who can find such a woman, the proverb asks, and the gospels answer with names: Mary Magdalene, the other Mary, Joanna, Susanna, and many others, who saw the death, the burial and the empty grave with their own eyes and were believed by the brethren because they were sent.

*Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.* (Proverbs 31:10)

cards.old_note: thread:women-as-the-first-witnesses-of-the-resurrection-and-the-faithful-witness-substance | *And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed.* The fear is the faithful-witness fear of the resurrection-substance breaking into the world.
cards.note: Matthew 28:8 — *And they departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy; and did run to bring his disciples word.* *And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.* (Mark 16:8) Mark tells how they trembled. Matthew shows the same fear and says it came with *great joy*, so they *did run to bring his disciples word*. Fear is in both accounts, and in Matthew it does not keep them from the errand they were sent on.

cards.member_note: Matthew 28:8 — *departed quickly from the sepulchre with fear and great joy.* Matthew keeps the women's fear but joins it to joy and a run to carry the word to the disciples.

cards.src_text: Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.
cards.tgt_text: And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.
cards.old_note: thread:women-as-the-first-witnesses-of-the-resurrection-and-the-faithful-witness-substance | The Matthean parallel of the women meeting the risen King.
cards.note: Matthew 28:9 — *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.* (Mark 16:9) Mark says he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. Matthew shows the meeting. As they went, Yahusha (Jesus) *met them*, and they *held him by the feet, and worshipped him*. The first to be seen by him are the women, and they take hold of him and worship.

cards.member_note: Matthew 28:9 — *they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* Matthew shows the women meeting the risen Yahusha (Jesus), taking hold of his feet and worshipping.

cards.old_note: thread:women-as-the-first-witnesses-of-the-resurrection-and-the-faithful-witness-substance | *Mary Magdalene as the first to whom the risen King appeared.* The framework's first-shall-be-last reversal walked out at the empty tomb (Yochanan/John 20:11-18).
cards.note: John 20:11 — *But Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre,* *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.* (Mark 16:9) Mark says he appeared first to Mary Magdalene. John shows how it went. She *stood without at the sepulchre weeping* and stooped to look in, and it is to her that Yahusha (Jesus) then speaks and sends. The first to be seen is the woman who would not leave the grave.
